_meta.notes: Hypotheses from the founder's papers; not verified demand. Lead poisoning is an expansion segment: complexation shown in solution chemistry, not yet in animals. Updated 24 Nov: radiation (lead segment) and lead poisoning (expansion) deepened with CDC, HHS REMM, ASPR pages and the TLC trial as context.

buyer_roles.title: Program manager, radiological/nuclear medical countermeasures (BARDA, ASPR/SNS, AFRRI)
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: stockpile buyers need an oral decorporation option beyond injected DTPA; the founder's papers report higher Pu/Am/U removal than DTPA in animals and oral tolerability in rats. BARDA is linked to OpenAlex works on radiation medical countermeasures. DTPA is FDA-approved for intravenous use against Am, Cm and Pu only (HHS REMM); ASPR and USUHS are also linked to OpenAlex works on radiation countermeasures.

buyer_roles.title: Paediatric toxicologist / poison-centre medical director
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis (expansion): CDC says no safe blood lead level in children has been identified; oral succimer lowered blood lead but did not improve cognition in the TLC trial, so the open question is what a children's study must show. Pb and Cd complexation by 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) is reported in solution chemistry only. NCEH, Cincinnati Children's and Uniklinik Aachen are linked to OpenAlex works on lead poisoning, a research signal and not purchase intent.

buyer_roles.title: Radiopharmaceutical business development lead
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: immuno-PET developers may want a 89Zr chelator that does not release 89Zr into bone; Zr-HOPO matched or surpassed DFO stability and showed 2.4%ID/g vs 17.0%ID/g bone uptake in mice.

buyer_roles.title: Contrast-agent R&D head (MRI gadolinium agents)
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: makers of gadolinium agents face regulator pressure over retention; the founder's gadolinium paper reports better Gd removal than DTPA. Guerbet, Bracco and Bayer are linked to OpenAlex works on gadolinium retention.

industries.name: Radiation countermeasures: government stockpiles and defense
industries.why: Hypothesis: the papers describe limited current therapies for radionuclide contamination and a dirty-bomb threat; HOPO ligands removed more actinides than DTPA in animal models. Not verified demand. DTPA is approved for intravenous use only (nebulised: adults only), and the Strategic National Stockpile is part of the federal response for radiological and nuclear threats.

industries.name: Radiopharmaceutical imaging (89Zr PET)
industries.why: Hypothesis: 89Zr released from DFO accumulates in bone; a more stable chelator could give a safer tracer.

industries.name: Gadolinium contrast-agent makers
industries.why: Hypothesis: regulators recommended discontinuing over half of approved gadolinium agents; a chelation remedy could sit alongside the product.

needs.text: Hypothesis: emergency planners and stockpile buyers need an oral, more effective alternative to injected DTPA. Reasoning: the papers report higher Pu, Am and U removal than DTPA in animals and oral tolerability in rats.

Hypothesis (expansion): paediatric lead teams need to know what a children's chelation study must show, since oral succimer already exists and lowered blood lead without improving cognition in the TLC trial. Reasoning: CDC reports no safe blood lead level in children; HOPO's lead evidence is binding chemistry only.
Hypothesis: PET developers need an 89Zr chelator that stays bound in vivo and conjugates to antibodies. Reasoning: Zr-HOPO matched or surpassed DFO and a bifunctional derivative exists.

Hypothesis: contrast-agent makers and MRI providers need a way to reduce gadolinium retention. Reasoning: 3,4,3-LI(1,2-HOPO) removed Gd better than DTPA in a preclinical study measured with a 153Gd radiotracer.

expansion_segments.name: Lead and heavy-metal poisoning in children (public health and paediatrics)
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis, early: the same ligand complexes Pb, Cd and Sn in solution chemistry, not yet in animals or people. CDC says no safe blood lead level in children has been identified, and oral succimer lowered blood lead without improving cognition in the TLC trial. Health departments, children's hospitals and NCEH/ATSDR are linked to OpenAlex works on lead poisoning, a research signal and not purchase intent.
